req.title: Task title max length
req.statement: The system shall respond with HTTP 422 when the title exceeds the maximum length constraint.

doc.reasoning: The requirement states the system shall respond with HTTP 422 when the task title exceeds the maximum length constraint. From schemas.py, TaskBase.title has max_length=100. Tests must cover: (1) positive case — title at exactly 100 chars accepted with HTTP 201, (2) negative case — title at 101 chars rejected with HTTP 422, (3) boundary case — title at 99 chars accepted with HTTP 201. Additional tests cover title at 0 chars (empty, rejected) and a clearly over-limit title (130 chars). The violation in test[3] was kind=negative with heuristic=EP; EP is valid for negative tests when the test represents a member of an invalid equivalence partition. To fix the violation, test[3] heuristic is changed from EP to NEG, which is the correct heuristic for a negative test exercising an invalid input partition well beyond the boundary. All other tests are preserved unchanged.

tests.name: test_create_task_title_exactly_max_length_accepted
preconditions: FastAPI app is running in-process via TestClient
Database is initialized with pre-loaded rows
actions: POST /tasks/ with title of exactly 100 characters and valid completed field
expected: Response body contains title field equal to the 100-char string
Response body contains id (integer) and completed=false
trace: R-TASK-029: max_length=100 in TaskBase.title; exactly 100 chars must be accepted
BVA: at-boundary value; catches off-by-one mutation max_length=100 -> max_length=99
tests.executable:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
from app.main import app

client = TestClient(app)
title_100 = "A" * 100

def test_create_task_title_exactly_max_length_accepted():
    payload = {"title": title_100, "completed": False}
    r = client.post("/tasks/", json=payload)
    assert r.status_code == 201
    body = r.json()
    assert body["title"] == title_100
    assert body["completed"] == False
    assert isinstance(body["id"], int)

test_create_task_title_exactly_max_length_accepted()
